dsi8-the-led-wall.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does the sanctuary wall go blurry? It goes blurry when it is fed less than it needs: a small image stretched big, a square image forced into the widescreen, or a plain HDMI 1.4 cable that tops out around 1080p. Feed it the full picture, about 2560 by 1440 in its 16:9 shape, over DVI or a higher-bandwidth input, and it stays sharp. Here is how the wall works.
dsi8-the-led-wall.example: ONE SLIDE, TWO WAYS. Say a volunteer makes a slide at 1920 by 1080 and sends it over plain HDMI 1.4. The wall is about 2560 by 1440, so that picture has to be stretched to fill it, and the fine P1.99mm wall shows every soft edge. Now make the same slide at 2560 by 1440, in the 16:9 shape, edge to edge, and send it over DVI or the higher-bandwidth input. Nothing has to be stretched, and the words stay sharp.
dsi8-the-led-wall.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the sanctuary wall go blurry? Because a fine P1.99mm wall shows every soft edge it is given. So give it none: send the picture by cable through the VX1000, not by NDI; use the higher-bandwidth input for the full resolution at 60 frames per second; and make every image at the wall's native size and 16:9 shape, edge to edge, never stretched. Then the vision is written plain, so the one who reads it may run (Habakkuk 2:2).
